We explore unsupervised speech generation through the application of contrastive learning, minimizing reliance on manually transcribed data. A significant bottleneck in the process involves parallel speech and text domains, often plagued by transcription errors or disparities. We address this challenge by employing a dual approach. First, to enhance our model's ability to recognize speech content, we create artificial parallel datasets utilizing combination techniques. Second, to rectify existing datasets, we develop a cross-modal alignment method to closely match speech and text signals. We have designed a novel unsupervised speech generation model that is able to learn this cross-modal similarity without labels, achieving this through the introduction of two contrastive losses. Experimental results demonstrate that this model performs significantly better on TTS metrics such as MOS, particularly when compared to models relying on inaccurate transcriptions, at a reduced training cost. The complete code can be found at https://github.com/m2e0/bot-lab-research/tree/master/contrastive_tts.

In understanding the universe's late-time evolution and the dark energy dominance, many theories have been formulated, with the fractional volume of space in holographic dark energy models representing one potential approach. This theoretical framework has been further developed by introducing complexity factors and nonlinear relationships, including the Tsallis law, to better comprehend these phenomena. This paper explores the evolution equation of a complex form of quintessence in holographic dark energy models and investigates their mathematical properties. These models are evaluated based on cosmological parameters and their impact on the acceleration of the universe's expansion, with the results showing that the fractional volume models can describe the universe's current acceleration and state.

Multi-objective optimization problems are ubiquitous in engineering and optimization, yet solving them efficiently remains a significant challenge, particularly when such problems involve a combination of continuous and discrete variables and complex non-linear relationships. This research seeks to tackle this issue by developing an innovative solution method that leverages a variation of the NSGAII algorithm, combining the principles of the original algorithm with key insights from branch and bound techniques to efficiently tackle the most critical decision variables in these optimization problems. To enhance solution quality, the proposed method incorporates a sophisticated local improvement process, refining variable selection criteria based on the number of non-dominated solutions at each iteration. This algorithm has been rigorously tested against demanding optimization problems, yielding consistently high-quality results. When compared to competing algorithms, such as MOEA/D-DE, PDEA3, and a hybrid NSGAII-DE approach, the proposed algorithm yields superior outcomes, as benchmarked on diverse test cases. Key performance metrics, including hypervolume and crowdedness, are used to evaluate solution sets, while a sensitivity analysis is conducted to assess the scalability of the proposed algorithm.

The specific definition of a Lie groupoid involves a pair consisting of a differential groupoid and a real number. However, this definition can be simplified by considering a single formula: a map from a sheaf of double points to the groupoid's space, which is differential and satisfies certain local conditions. This formula defines a Lie groupoid and serves as the primary definition of the concept. It is demonstrated that the traditional definition implies this formula and that the formula generates an equivalence between certain categories. The concept of integration of a groupoid is defined by a map that selects leaves from a groupoid satisfying a differential condition. The example of a curve on a manifold demonstrates that this selection may not always exist universally. However, it is proved that the selection does exist for certain special types of groupoids and that their leaves have smooth properties even when the original curve does not have smooth properties. Additionally, it is shown that the concept of a linked groupoid encompasses these types of groupoids and the selection of its leaves can be defined within these groups. The example of a 2-dimensional sphere demonstrates that the selection of its leaves can also have singular properties even within these groups.

In recent years, the quantifiable model has gained momentum as a preferred data analysis approach due to its ability to process complex systems. Despite this, researchers face significant hurdles when attempting to build and run complex models, including the challenge of gathering and organizing diverse data sets, as well as addressing corresponding software applications. The disparity between the speed of scientific discoveries and the advancement of infrastructure to support them is a long-standing issue. The distribution and processing of digital content, particularly for data-driven applications, places extraordinary demands on existing networks.

Advances in network technology, specifically with the emergence of 5G, may help alleviate these challenges in the distribution of digital content by enabling faster data transfer rates and reduced latency. However, this will only address part of the problem, and existing disparities will persist unless the flow of digital content is managed by a dedicated cyberinfrastructure. Cyberinfrastructure cyberinfrastructure is a collection of resources, including hardware, software, and data, with defined protocols and services, designed to support seamless access and coordination. The flow of content will become even more crucial with the advent of edge computing.

Within healthcare and life science research, specific applications such as biomedical informatics depend heavily on the flow of digital content to support data analysis. The quantifiable model approach, particularly with the advent of precision medicine, has become a staple in data analysis. The ability to gather and process corresponding data will play a crucial role in delivering personalized treatments and developing novel therapies. The application of aspect-based sentiment analysis continues to hold significance in understanding consumer reviews, despite the challenges presented by context-dependent sentiment expressions and limited training data for specific domains and cultures. Existing approaches often rely on word or phrase representations, ignoring the nuanced context dependencies. This limitation is addressed through the use of a more comprehensive framework for sentiment representation. To bridge this gap, a novel pre-training technique for sentiment analysis, incorporating supervised contrastive pre-training, is proposed for improving aspect-specific sentiment representation. By leveraging a supervised pre-training approach, a more effective learning outcome is achieved across various domain and cultural settings. An additional strategy for incorporating contrastive learning across related but differently labeled data is also introduced. Experimental findings on widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate the benefits of this proposed approach, exceeding the performance of standard word-level sentiment analysis models in multiple aspects.

Researchers interested in understanding how risk factors influence health outcomes often employ mediation analysis, and this paper explores its application in studies involving case-control samples, focusing specifically on data analyzed through logistic regression. Given that case-control sampling typically yields biased estimates of direct and indirect effect parameters, the paper addresses the challenge of estimating these effects without restricting participants' observed characteristics. It proposes a computation method for logistic regression mediation analysis, taking into account a binary mediator, and provides identification conditions as well as conditions under which the results generalize to partial identification situations. The method presents a convex optimization problem whose solution provides a set of confidence intervals for the parameters of interest. The proposed estimation technique is through convex optimization of a loss function and does not necessitate specific distributional assumptions, offering a universal solution. The method is evaluated using data from the National Transplant Offices based in Madrid, specifically in regards to how potential scarcity of organ donors affects families' support for donor consent, and the results demonstrate that women are more likely than men to experience increased support as a result of discussing the issue with their families.

This research delves into secure communication networks with multiple users that incorporate reconfigurable intelligent surfaces to enhance stability and improve security. Since these surfaces have practical limitations, we investigate their optimal deployment strategies under two models of hardware imperfections - a uniform model where all surfaces share all secrets and a dispersed model where each surface exclusively knows its corresponding secret. For the case where all surfaces share secrets, we develop an algorithm that leverages the stacking of secrecy threats and an iterative weighted method to optimize the phase shifts. On the other hand, for the scenario where each surface has its unique secret, we propose a decentralized approach that leverages the stacking of secrecy threats and an iterative method to optimize the phase shifts, utilizing a random strategy to bypass the dependence on the intercardinal problem. Simulation results confirm that our proposed solutions can efficiently optimize the RIS to achieve higher objectives such as the minimum average interference to the neighboring user and the minimum correlation between the transmitted signals.

In the realm of distributed AI, enhancing the functionality of perception through resampling and relabeling can significantly contribute to this goal.  While there are numerous methods for refining perception, a common challenge arises from the fact that training data often lacks sufficient diversity, necessitating a way to amplify it without increasing the training cost.  Furthermore, increased variability in data can complicate the process of adjusting models, which may lead to decreased accuracy.  This research introduces an innovative mechanism, the contrastive value strategy, specifically designed to tackle these challenges.  By leveraging this strategy, we can obtain improved accuracy on existing models, without increasing the training cost.  We achieve this by amplifying dataset diversity through resampling and relabeling, which in turn facilitates a more effective training process.  In comparison to existing approaches, our method excels by incorporating a comprehensive dataset diversity design, alongside a more sophisticated resampling strategy that prioritizes easy-to-hard attributes, along with an efficient relabeling mechanism based on the concepts outlined in the "Fourier Sum" law.  In addition, our method identifies opportunities for improved data utilization within existing models, which may have been overlooked by previous methods.  Ultimately, the proposed method enables both model and perception augmentation, which ultimately contributes to the broader goal of enhancing distributed AI.

The solar wind's pattern of acceleration and deceleration in the inner solar system is not fully understood and researchers are studying this phenomenon using data from the Parker Solar Probe's first outreach period. Specifically, they analyzed the plasma and magnetic field conditions near the and solar wind speed. Over a eight-day period in 2018, the solar wind exhibited an unusual pattern where the plasma density and magnetic field decreased while the speed increased. This pattern, though present in some periods, was otherwise filled with recurring low-frequency oscillations known as solar wind variances. These oscillations, which are more prevalent during periods of density and magnetic field decreases, may contribute to the plasma's low-frequency oscillations. The plasma and magnetic field patterns also showed an interesting correlation during one particular phase of the solar cycle. According to the current theory of heliospheric plasma dynamics, the solar wind's speed should decrease in conjunction with the density and magnetic field. However, the observed plasma and magnetic field conditions are more prone to high-frequency variations. This pattern, though present in some periods, was otherwise filled with recurring low-frequency oscillations known as the solar wind's pressure. These oscillations, which are more prevalent during periods of density and magnetic field decreases, may be less subject to high-frequency oscillations. The solar wind's low-speed period, which is more prone to low-frequency oscillations, may be less subject to high-frequency oscillations. We examine the notion of noncommutative principal countable bundles, which are constructed as a result of action by countable discrete groups on C*-algebras. Our investigation seeks to clarify under what conditions this action yields a suspension or orbit space. Specifically, we demonstrate that when a group acts faithfully on a C*-algebra with compact spectra, the resulting orbit space exhibits compactness. Furthermore, when a group acts faithfully on a C*-algebras with non-trivial spectra, the resulting orbit space is found to be homeomorphic to a suspension. A key example illustrates that faithful action does not necessarily result in a Gelfand spectrum that is homeomorphic to that of a suspension. Moreover, several counterexamples are provided to illustrate that the conditions identified do not necessarily generalize to the case of actions by non-discrete groups.

We show that any family of thin sets can be combined with a specific ultrafilter to create a sequence whose members, when grouped using this ultrafilter, have unique combinations. This outcome has two key implications: first, there are sets of natural numbers that can be combined in this way; second, it follows that there is a possible extension to the real number system where each possible grouping using an ultrafilter results in distinct values. Furthermore, this result helps resolve an ongoing debate concerning the possibility of creating a subset of natural numbers where each possible grouping using an ultrafilter results in distinct values. Apart from this, we also prove that there are possible extensions to the real number system where certain key properties are satisfied: the sum of the members of any family of numbers grouped using an ultrafilter is always less than or equal to 1.

The optical manifold in an optomechanical system that has been modified with $q$-deformation is investigated in this study.  Two types of linear propagation are examined, one propagated by the optical manifold in the stationary frame and the other propagated by the optical cavity in the moving frame.  The inverse Cherenkov effect occurs when the optical manifold in the stationary frame is excited, resulting in a negative group velocity of light, and we find that this effect becomes more pronounced as the deformation parameter increases.  On the other hand, when the optical cavity in the moving frame is excited, it exhibits normal dispersion and the ability to amplify a light signal, and we find that this amplification ratio maximizes at a specific value of the deformation parameter.  Furthermore, we find that both the spectral bandwidth and the signal-to-noise ratio of the light signal increase as the deformation parameter reaches a certain value, suggesting a maximum level of amplification and clarity that can be achieved in this system.

In the Half-Superfluid and Half-Metal phases of a Deformed Superfluid, described by the Dual-Rotors model, the Deformed Rotors transition to their scrambled forms by adopting a configuration adverse to R-parity in both even and odd dimensions. For even dimensions, this scrambled state features a simple structure characterized by a single Deformed Rotor with minimal excitation, whereas in odd dimensions, the scrambled Deformed Rotors exhibit a ground state with equally sized core and halo. In both cases, R-parity adverse transitions occur at lower points on the phase diagram, distinct from the 1s0+ state which marks the Superfluid to Deformed Superfluid phase shift. To diagnose these states, the authors propose the Scissors modes as indicators, which emerge as a consequence of the Deformed Rotors' scrambling and become visible in the Euclidean correlator as localized peaks.

A novel method for addressing first-order nonlinear hyperbolic PDEs through cell-mean based neural networks demonstrates exceptional results, even in the presence of shocks and smooth solutions. The approach is also adaptable to higher-dimensional problems and intrinsic difficulties with the frame transformation can be mitigated. The existing method relies on a specific type of activation function, ensuring that cell-mean values serve as key thresholds within the network. This insight enables the construction of solutions as a combination of cell-mean neural networks. The same method can be used for parabolic PDEs with similar efficiency. The framework's flexibility is demonstrated through numerical examples involving both shockwave and smooth solutions to the Burgers equation, as well as the FitzHugh-Nagumo equation.

In addition to enhancing sensitivity, the LHC pp and p-Pb programs during Run 3 will yield valuable data on these systems, complemented by the first ever p-O and Ar-Gd collisions. A private and public funding initiative, focused on enhancing the ALICE experiment's capabilities, will facilitate installation of a cutting-edge luminometer, a novel calorimeter, and the enhancement of an existing system.
